title: Automated issue-triage workflows must only act on label-less issues
answers: workflow adds labels to issues that already have labels
triage bot overwrote maintainer labels on an issue
how do I make an issue automation only run on new unlabeled issues
label automation on issue opened event guard
body:
Invariant: a workflow that auto-labels issues must run only when the issue has no labels yet, so it never overrides labels a maintainer or issue form already set.
Enforced by: .github/workflows/triage.yml:jobs.label.if, which checks `github.event.issue.labels[0] == null` alongside the `github.repository == 'mlflow/mlflow'` repo guard.
Trigger is `issues: types: [opened]` only, so later edits or relabels do not re-run it.
If the guard is dropped or moved, the job re-labels issues that were already triaged and can add labels that conflict with the maintainer's choice.
The job also has `concurrency` keyed on the issue number, so repeated events for one issue do not race.
applies: Any new GitHub Actions workflow in this repo that edits labels or other metadata on issues.
says: The automated triage bot is overwriting labels manually assigned by project maintainers.
Prevent the issue categorization workflow from tagging tickets that already have labels.
Automated triage should only apply tags to newly opened, completely unlabeled issues.
The issue triage bot replaced our custom tags when an issue was updated.
Stop the automated triage system from modifying labels on previously categorized tickets.
search: Automated issue-triage workflows that apply labels must run only on newly opened issues that have no existing labels to prevent overwriting maintainer selections. In .github/workflows/triage.yml:jobs.label.if, this is enforced by checking github.event.issue.labels[0] == null alongside the github.repository == 'mlflow/mlflow' guard. The workflow triggers strictly on issues: types: [opened] and uses concurrency keyed on the issue number to prevent races.
